Analysis of Bus Operator Platform Operational Load

This analysis evaluates the operational load on the bus operator platform based on the dataset gathered from business events. The dataset spans from November 27, 2025, to February 19, 2026, encompassing a total of 14,985 events across 109 different event types.

1. VOLUME PROFILE

The total volume of events recorded is entirely application-driven, with all 14,985 events categorized under the "application" category. This indicates that user interactions with the application are the sole contributors to the operational load, with no system-driven events (such as push or sync events) recorded in this dataset.

2. CRITICAL LOAD

Identifying the specific events that generate the most traffic reveals the following counts:

  • viewed_hisab_page: 5,361 events (35.78%)
  • viewed_hisab_bus_detail: 3,159 events (21.08%)
  • viewed_dashboard_page: 1,403 events (9.36%)
  • viewed_hisab_trip_detail: 1,275 events (8.51%)
  • clicked_hisab_trip_detail_card: 1,205 events (8.04%)
  • clicked_hisab_bus_detail_card: 1,141 events (7.61%)
  • clicked_nav_drawer_menu: 131 events (0.87%)
  • clicked_hisab_yestarday_btn: 125 events (0.83%)
  • dashboard_clicked_gps_vistar_se_dekhe_bus_card: 90 events (0.60%)
  • home_page_load_error: 88 events (0.59%)

These top events account for a significant portion of the total traffic, with the "viewed_hisab_page" alone constituting over one-third of all events.

3. INFRASTRUCTURE IMPACT

The analysis of peaks and total volume indicates that the system is heavily reliant on user interactions with the application. Given the high volume of events, particularly during peak usage times, the system must be capable of handling substantial traffic efficiently. The current data suggests that scalability needs are critical, especially if user engagement continues to grow. The absence of system-driven events implies that there may be opportunities to optimize backend processes to better manage load, such as implementing efficient caching strategies or enhancing server capacity to accommodate spikes in user activity.
